description: Verify that DUT validates the ICMP checksum and silently discards Echo Requests whose checksum is wrong — no Reply, no error message (RFC 792 'Checksum field is checked')
approach:
[Objective]
A wrong ICMP checksum means the message is corrupt; silently dropping is the only safe action. DUT must NOT reply (the contents can't be trusted) and must NOT generate ICMP error (which would also need the corrupt header).

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: ICMP Echo Request with an intentionally wrong checksum value

2. Observation (5 s window):
   • DUT → Tester: nothing — no Echo Reply, no error message

[Pass condition]
DUT does not emit any ICMP traffic within the window.

[Fail condition]
Fail_dut_replied — DUT emitted some response despite the bad checksum. Indicates the receive path skipped checksum verification.

verdicts.Pass: DUT silently dropped the bad-checksum Request — normal
verdicts.Fail_dut_replied: DUT replied despite invalid ICMP checksum — checksum verification skipped
